title: Iowa football CFP rooting guide: What Hawkeyes hope for in Week 11

 Scout Springgate Hawkeyes Wire Updated Nov. 14, 2026, 1:20 p.m. ET Hear this story As Iowa football (7-2, 4-2 Big Ten) clashes with Purdue (3-6, 2-4 Big Ten) at a sold-out Kinnick Stadium on Saturday, Hawkeye fans will also be keeping their eye on the out-of-town scoreboards, as Iowa is within reach of securing its first-ever College Football Playoff appearance.
 While a 10-2 finish for the 15th-ranked Hawkeyes would put Iowa in an excellent position to clinch a spot in the 12-team CFP field, Kirk Ferentz and Co. would welcome help around the nation to improve its CFP standing.
 As the Hawkeyes look to bolster their resume with a win over the Boilermakers, here is what Iowa fans should be rooting for elsewhere this weekend:
 Week 11 College Football Schedule
 Duke at No. 7 Miami Saturday, 11 a.m. CTABC Root for : Duke 
 A second-straight loss increases the odds that the ACC is a one-bid league. Hawkeye fans should be pulling for Duke here.
 No. 13 Wake Forest at SMU Saturday, 11 a.m. CTESPN Root for : SMU 
 Like Miami, a Wake Forest loss increases the odds that the ACC is a one-bid league. A Wake Forest loss all but guarantees another Iowa rise in the rankings.
 Northwestern at No. 20 Ohio State Saturday, 11 a.m. CTFox Root for : Northwestern 
 After an embarrassing home loss to Oregon last week, Ohio State's playoff chances are on life support. A fourth loss for the Buckeyes would be the proverbial "nail in the coffin" for Ohio State and would remove them from impacting Iowa. Iowa fans should be cheering on the Wildcats.
 No. 3 Alabama at Vanderbilt Saturday, 11:45 a.m. CTSEC Network Root for: Vanderbilt 
 As much as the CFP committee likes this two-loss Crimson Tide team, a third loss to Vanderbilt would be catastrophic for Alabama's playoff outlook.
 --> No. 8 Tennessee at Texas A&M Saturday, 2 p.m. CTESPN Root for : Texas A&M 
 With two losses, Tennessee and Iowa may be more alike than not, and a loss to a middling Texas A&M squad would be a major blow to the Volunteers' resume.
 No. 22 Missouri at No. 1 Georgia Saturday, 2:30 p.m. CTABC Root for: Georgia 
 Missouri isn't a threat at the moment, but a win at Georgia changes that in a hurry. A loss would eliminate Missouri from CFP contention.
 Boston College at No. 5 Notre Dame Saturday, 2:30 p.m. CTNBC Root for: Boston College 
 It's a long shot, but if the Irish drop two of their final three games, then Notre Dame is likely on the outside looking in of the College Football Playoff. Notre Dame closes versus Boston College, versus SMU, and at Syracuse. SMU could be tricky, but the Irish dropping either game against Boston College or Syracuse would be a major upset.
 No. 18 USC at No. 9 Indiana Saturday, 2:30 p.m. CTCBS Root for: Indiana 
 A USC win could be one of the first dominoes toward Iowa reaching the Big Ten championship game, but a third loss by USC likely means the Trojans are boxed out of the CFP. There's a chance for USC to impress in its regular-season finale at UCLA, but, after a loss here, the Trojans would be too far down the rankings to make the climb back up inside the CFP field.
 Michigan at No. 16 Oregon Saturday, 2:30 p.m. CTFS1 Root for: Michigan 
 If the Wolverines hand Oregon a fourth loss, the Ducks will be eliminated from CFP contention.
 Florida at No. 11 Kentucky Saturday, 5:15 p.m. CTESPN Root for: Florida 
 The Gators could hand Kentucky a third loss, and seriously damage the Wildcats' CFP chances. A Florida win guarantees an Iowa climb in the CFP rankings.
 Baylor at No. 10 BYU Saturday, 6 p.m. CTFox Root for: Baylor 
 Baylor could bounce BYU out of the CFP picture by handing the Cougars a third loss.\
 No. 6 Texas at No. 21 LSU Saturday, 6:30 p.m. CTABC Root for: LSU 
 There's a good argument to be made both ways here, but an LSU win hands Texas its third loss and gives Iowa a chance to jump the Longhorns. Iowa shouldn't think only about getting in. Is there a path to rise all the way to No. 8 and host a CFP game? A Texas loss could help take Iowa there. Texas closes against Arkansas and at Texas A&M, so this is the best final chance for Texas to drop another game.
 Meanwhile, LSU certainly reenters the CFP discussion with a signature win over Texas, but the Tigers wouldn't be out of the woods either. LSU has a tough road trip to Tennessee next week where the Vols could bounce the Tigers out of the CFP discussion.
 No. 17 South Carolina at Arkansas Saturday, 6:45 p.m. CTSEC Network Root for: Arkansas 
 We're calling the Hogs. Get South Carolina out of the equation.
 No. 12 Texas Tech at No. 25 Oklahoma State Saturday, 8:30 p.m. CTESPN Root for: Oklahoma State 
 An Oklahoma State win creates another clear avenue for Iowa to rise in the rankings.
 No. 2 Utah at No. 23 Arizona Saturday, 9:30 p.m. CTFox Root for: Utah 
 Utah is unbeaten and in prime position to grab at least one bid out of the Big 12. A Utes victory ends Arizona's CFP hopes.
 No. 19 Ole Miss at Oklahoma Sunday, Noon CTSEC Network Root for: Oklahoma 
 With an Oklahoma win, the Sooners can end any hopes for Trinidad Chambliss and Ole Miss returning to the CFP.
